metadata.title: OSS Radar — what's trending on GitHub
metadata.description: See which GitHub projects, programming languages and developers are trending right now. Simple rankings for everyone, updated daily.

theme.toggle: Switch between light and dark theme

footer.text: Data comes from GitHub's public search and is refreshed every day. This site is not run by GitHub.

grades.formula: Activity score = (commits × 3 + merged PRs × 2 + closed issues) ÷ ln(stars + 1), over the last 30 days.

home.title: What's hot in {domain}
home.intro: The most active open-source projects on GitHub, and the libraries they build with. Updated daily.
home.scope: Tracking {repos, plural, one {# project} other {# projects}} and {libs, plural, one {# library} other {# libraries}}. Data for {month}.

highlights.label: At a glance
highlights.mostActive: <link>{name}</link> is the most active project: {commits, plural, one {# commit} other {# commits}} and {prs, plural, one {# merged PR} other {# merged PRs}} in the last 30 days.
highlights.mostStarred: <link>{name}</link> has the most stars among projects that are still active: {stars}.
highlights.topGrowing: <link>{name}</link> is the fastest-growing library: used by {count, plural, one {# project} other {# projects}}, up {rate} from last month.
highlights.topUsed: <link>{name}</link> is the most-used library: {count, plural, one {# project depends} other {# projects depend}} on it.

projects.title: Which projects are most active?
projects.description: A longer bar means more is going on. Activity counts commits, merged pull requests and closed issues from the last 30 days, adjusted for project size.

libs.title: Which libraries do they build with?
libs.description: The longer the bar, the more of the tracked projects depend on that library.
libs.baselineNote: Growth needs two months of data. It appears after next month's crawl.
libs.noGrowth: No library has grown since last month.

radar.title: Every project on one map
radar.description: Each dot is a project. The further right, the more stars. The higher, the more work in the last 30 days.

repositories.title: Search projects
repositories.description: Find one of {count} popular open-source projects. Type a word, or narrow the list with the filters.
repositories.criteria: The list has the 30 most-starred projects of each of the six fields, checked every day. Lists, courses and tutorials are left out.

search.label: Search
search.help: Looks at project names, descriptions and languages. Use more than one word to narrow it down.

language.label: Language
language.help: The main language the project is written in.

activity.label: Activity
activity.help: Activity shows how much work happened in the last 30 days: updates, merged changes and closed issues, adjusted for how big the project is.

summary.none: No filters yet, so you are seeing everything.

noMatch.title: No project matches these filters
noMatch.description: Try a different word, or remove one of the filters below.

how.source: Where the projects come from: for each of the six fields we take the 30 most-starred projects on GitHub that carry that field's topic (frontend, backend, devops, mobile, data-science, security).
how.excluded: What we leave out: collections of links, courses and tutorials, such as awesome lists, roadmaps and interview guides, because they are not software.
how.activity: Activity: we count the updates, merged changes and closed issues from the last 30 days and adjust for how popular the project is.
how.fields: A project can belong to more than one field. It is shown once, with all of its fields.
how.fresh: Refreshed once a day from GitHub's public data.

repositories.error: Couldn't load the projects. Make sure the backend is running, then reload.

empty.title: No projects yet
empty.description: Projects appear after the first crawl. Start one and reload the page.

errors.title: Something went wrong
errors.description: This page couldn't load its data. Try again, or check that the backend is running.
errors.notFoundDescription: That page doesn't exist or has moved.

levels.title: How active are these projects?
levels.description: Every tracked project, grouped by its activity over the last 30 days. Darker amber means more active.

languages.title: What are they written in?
languages.description: The main language of each project.

hero.title: What's hot on GitHub right now
hero.subtitle: The projects, languages and people rising on GitHub. Refreshed every day, so there is always something new.

explainer.summary: New to GitHub? Tap here to see what these words mean

github.text: A website where people share the code (the instructions) that makes apps and games work.

project.text: One project on GitHub, like a folder that holds everything about one app or tool. Programmers also call it a repository, or repo.

star.text: A star is a like. The more stars, the more people find it useful.

developer.text: A person or a team who writes code.

hot.title: Most-starred projects
hot.description: Stars are likes, so these are the projects people like the most. Pick how old the projects can be.
hot.empty: No new projects to show yet.
hot.rule: Projects with the most stars right now. Choose a period to see only projects that started recently, or choose Any time to include older ones. Lists, courses and tutorials are left out.

loved.title: Favorites that are still going strong
loved.description: Projects with lots of stars that were also updated in the last month.
loved.rule: The most-starred projects among the top 30 of each field that were also updated in the last 30 days.

languages.title: Which programming languages are popular?
languages.description: A programming language is what developers write code in. The longer the bar, the more new popular projects use it this month.
languages.note: We count projects started in the last 30 days that have at least 50 stars.
languages.rule: For each language we count the projects started in the last 30 days that have at least 50 stars.

glance.chartTitle: Which language builds the most new popular projects?

languages.ruleWeek: For each language we count the projects started in the last 7 days that have at least 10 stars.
languages.ruleAll: For each language we count every project, however old, that has more than 1,000 stars. This shows which languages have the most well-loved projects overall.

developers.title: People and teams to watch
developers.description: Who is building the hot projects, and who has the most followers. Up to 100 people in each list.
developers.hotProjects: {count, plural, one {# hot project} other {# hot projects}}
developers.publicProjects: {count, plural, one {# public project} other {# public projects}}
developers.followersHelp: Followers are people who keep up with this developer's work.
developers.rule: Behind the hot projects: the owners of the most-starred projects for the age you pick (last 7 days, last 30 days, or any time). Most followed: people with over 5,000 followers who share public projects.

glance.risingTitle: Who is behind the hottest new projects?

fields.title: Browse by field
fields.description: Pick a field to see its most popular projects.

repo.startedMonthsAgo: {months, plural, one {Started 1 month ago} other {Started # months ago}}
repo.startedYearsAgo: {years, plural, one {Started 1 year ago} other {Started # years ago}}
repo.perDayHelp: Stars earned per day on average since it started

how.summary: How do we decide these rankings?
how.intro: GitHub has no official trending list, so we build ours from GitHub's public search. Everything is updated once a day.
how.newProjects: Most-starred projects: the projects with the most stars right now. You can limit them to ones started in the last 7 or 30 days, or look at all of them.
how.loved: Favorites: projects with the most stars that were also updated in the last 30 days.
how.languages: Languages: how many projects started in the last 30 days earned at least 50 stars, for each language. The percentage is each language's share among the languages shown.
how.developers: People and teams: the owners of the hot new projects, and the developers with the most followers.
